title: Two roots: work placed on the machine that has the data, reports flow home
persona: A developer with two machines at home: their main computer and a 'lab machine'. Short messages, doesn't know file paths on the lab machine.

peers.name: lab
peers.note: the lab machine: holds the company sales data (sales/ folder) and the big disk

goals: Get an analysis of the sales data that lives on the lab machine: total revenue per region (units x unit_price) and the best month, saved as a markdown report next to the data on the lab machine. You don't know the exact path, only that the data is on the lab machine.
Meanwhile on this home computer: get a tiny python script that prints a greeting for a given name, with pytest tests, in a folder named greet.
Finally ask which region had the most revenue and how much.
script: Ask for the sales analysis first, mentioning it's on the lab machine.
Then ask for the greet script.
Wait for main to come back; ask the final question; finish.

checks.name: report written on the lab root
analysis ran as a proxy on lab
checks.title: sales|revenue|analy

checks.name: greet tests pass on home
checks.cmd: cd greet && python3 -m pytest -q >/tmp/pytest.$$.out 2>&1 && echo PYTEST-OK || tail -5 /tmp/pytest.$$.out
